$comment: The OptiAI skill library. Every entry has a folder beside this file holding its SKILL.md. Vendored entries are copied verbatim from the upstream repository (SKILL.md and any references/ folder only); OptiAI-authored entries are written here. Nothing outside this list is installable.

skills.name: Caveman
skills.summary: Ultra-compressed replies: drops filler and articles, keeps every technical fact.
skills.detail: The model answers like a terse senior engineer - no preamble, no hedging, no restating the question - while keeping code, paths, numbers and error text exact. Levels lite, full and ultra trade readability for savings. Best for long coding sessions where output tokens dominate the bill.
skills.author: Julius Brussee

skills.name: Caveman Commit
skills.summary: Conventional Commits messages compressed to intent only.
skills.detail: Subject under 50 characters, body only when the why is not obvious from the diff. Fires on 'write a commit' or 'commit message' so the model never pads a commit with a diary of what it did.
skills.author: Julius Brussee

skills.name: Caveman Review
skills.summary: Code review as one line per finding: location, problem, fix.
skills.detail: Cuts review noise to the actionable signal. Each comment names the file and line, what is wrong, and the change that fixes it. Use for PR review, diff review, or 'what is wrong with this'.
skills.author: Julius Brussee

skills.name: Ponytail
skills.summary: Forces the laziest solution that actually works: YAGNI, standard library first, one line before fifty.
skills.detail: Channels a senior developer who has seen everything. Questions whether the task needs to exist, reaches for platform features before dependencies, and refuses speculative abstraction. Levels lite, full and ultra. Applies to writing, refactoring, reviewing and choosing libraries.
skills.author: Dietrich Gebert

skills.name: Ponytail Review
skills.summary: Review that only hunts over-engineering: what to delete and what replaces it.
skills.detail: Finds reinvented standard library, unneeded dependencies, speculative abstractions and dead flexibility. One line per finding. Complements a correctness review rather than replacing it.
skills.author: Dietrich Gebert

skills.name: Emil Design Engineering
skills.summary: Emil Kowalski's philosophy on UI polish, component design and the invisible details that make software feel great.
skills.detail: Opinionated guidance on when to animate and when not to, easing and duration, touch targets, focus states, layering, and the small decisions that separate polished interfaces from adequate ones. Long skill; enable it for UI-heavy projects.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: Animate
skills.summary: Build an animation from scratch by making the decisions in the right order: whether, why, which tool, which properties, which curve.
skills.detail: Walks from 'should this animate at all' through purpose, technique, properties, easing, duration, interruption and exit, then writes the implementation. Use for transitions, motion on components, and making interfaces feel alive.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: Apple Design
skills.summary: Apple's approach to interface design and physical motion, translated for the web.
skills.detail: Gesture-driven UI, springs, sheets and drags, momentum and interruptible transitions, translucent materials, typography, reduced motion and the foundations of feedback, spatial consistency and restraint. Long skill; enable for products that want an Apple-like feel.
skills.author: Emil Kowalski

skills.name: Tasteful Output
skills.summary: Prose without AI slop: marketing copy, taglines, README narrative, naming and positioning that read like a person wrote them.
skills.detail: Applies when word choice shapes perception. Bans the tells of generated text, insists on concrete nouns and specific claims, and keeps the voice consistent. Not for code, data or structured output.
skills.author: dnh33

skills.name: Anti-slop Audit
skills.summary: Reviews existing text for the tells of AI-generated copy and says exactly what to cut.
skills.detail: For landing pages, README prose, pitch decks and product descriptions. Triggers on 'audit this copy', 'does this sound like AI', 'tighten this up'. Returns findings, not a rewrite, unless asked.
skills.author: dnh33

skills.name: Graphify
skills.summary: Answers codebase questions from a persistent knowledge graph instead of grepping raw files.
skills.detail: Turns code, docs and papers into a graph with god nodes and communities, then routes architecture and relationship questions through graphify query, path and explain. Needs the graphify CLI installed (pip install graphifyy) and a graphify-out/ folder in the project. Long skill; the model only loads it when the question is about the codebase.
skills.author: Graphify Labs
skills.tokenImpact: -50% on codebase questions once a graph exists

skills.name: Super-mem
skills.summary: Persistent memory across sessions through the Supermemory CLI: store facts, search them later, forget what is stale.
skills.detail: Teaches the agent when to store a preference or decision, when to search before asking, and how to prune outdated memories. Needs the sm CLI (npm i -g supermemory-cli) and a Supermemory API key. Without them the skill is instructions with nothing to call.
skills.author: franksde

skills.name: Handoff.md Creator
skills.summary: Writes a HANDOFF.md a stranger can act on: verified state, next steps, decisions, traps, how to run.
skills.detail: Runs git status, log and the tests before writing, then produces a fixed-section handoff under 150 lines with file paths instead of pasted code. Use at the end of a session or when passing work to another person or agent.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: SQL Queries
skills.summary: Writes, explains and optimizes SQL against the real schema, with the plan read before any tuning advice.
skills.detail: Finds the schema in the repo first, names the dialect, parameterizes values, and ships every UPDATE or DELETE with the SELECT that shows what it touches. Optimization starts from EXPLAIN, not from guesses.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: Technical Doc Writer
skills.summary: READMEs, setup guides, API references, architecture notes and runbooks grounded in the actual code.
skills.detail: Decides the audience first, copies exact names from the code, uses tables for anything with three or more attributes, and runs every command it documents. House style over textbook style.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: Research Brief
skills.summary: Investigates a question and returns a decision-ready brief where every claim carries a dated source.
skills.detail: Restates the question as a decision, fixes the criteria before searching, prefers primary sources, verifies anything that changes the recommendation, and lists what could not be confirmed. Table over prose for comparisons.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: Frontend Engineering
skills.summary: Web UI work that matches the codebase, handles every state, and is accessible by default.
skills.detail: Reads neighbouring components before writing, uses the project's design tokens, enumerates empty, loading, error and success states as requirements, and treats keyboard access and contrast as non-negotiable. Covers React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte and plain DOM.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: Backend Engineering
skills.summary: Server code designed around how it fails: validation at the boundary, typed errors, transactions, timeouts, observability.
skills.detail: Traces the existing request path before adding to it, keeps auth where the resource is loaded, makes jobs idempotent, and writes down the rollback for every data change. Correct status codes and one structured log line per request.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: API Design
skills.summary: HTTP and RPC contracts that are obvious to use, hard to misuse and possible to change: naming, shapes, errors, pagination, versioning.
skills.detail: Starts from client use cases rather than tables, fixes one error shape and one casing, uses cursor pagination, treats breaking changes as a new major version, and delivers an endpoint table with examples and an OpenAPI fragment.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: Code Craft
skills.summary: General coding discipline: understand before changing, small focused diffs, match conventions, test what changed, verify before claiming done.
skills.detail: The baseline for any coding task without a more specific skill. Insists on a reproduction before a fix, one logical change per diff, reuse of existing helpers, a failing-then-passing test, and a summary that says what was verified and how.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: Prompt Porter
skills.summary: Writes and adapts prompts for other platforms: ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, custom GPTs, Cursor rules, system prompts, agents and image models.
skills.detail: Builds every prompt from the same eight parts, then applies each platform's conventions - XML tags for Claude, parameters last for Midjourney, short imperative bullets for rule files. Always delivers the prompt in a copyable block with a test input.
skills.author: OptiAI

skills.name: Spec Writer
skills.summary: Turns an idea or fuzzy request into a spec an engineer can build from: problem, scope, testable requirements, acceptance criteria.
skills.detail: Separates the problem from the proposed solution, checks the existing codebase for constraints, marks inferences so they can be corrected, and ends with the smallest version worth shipping. Keeps the whole document readable in ten minutes.
skills.author: OptiAI
